Main.sentence: Moneygall ( ___E:Irish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_language)___ : Muine Gall , meaning 'foreigners' ___E:thicket U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thicket)___ ')  is a village in ___E:County Offaly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Offaly)___ , bordering ___E:County Tipperary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Tipperary)___ , in Ireland.

It is situated on the ___E:R445 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R445_road_(Ireland))___ road between ___E:Dublin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin)___ and ___E:Limerick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limerick)___ .
There were 374 people living in the village as of the ___E:2022 census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_census_of_Ireland)___ .

Moneygall has a ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church)___ church, motorway service station, a car sales and repair centre, a ___E:national school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_school_(Ireland))___ , a ___E:Garda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garda_S%C3%ADoch%C3%A1na)___ station and a pub.  The nearest ___E:Church of Ireland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Ireland)___ church, Borrisnafarney, is 2 km from the village beside the former Loughton Demesne.

The village received international attention for being the ancestral home of Falmouth Kearney, a maternal great-great-great-grandfather of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ .
Obama visited the village in 2011.
Moneygall is in the ___E:Dáil constituency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%A1il_constituencies)___ of ___E:Offaly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offaly_(D%C3%A1il_constituency))___ .

It was previously in the constituency of ___E:Laois-Offaly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laois%E2%80%93Offaly_(D%C3%A1il_constituency))___ and was one term in the ___E:Tipperary North Dáil constituency U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tipperary_North_(D%C3%A1il_constituency))___ .

Moneygall is on the ___E:R445 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R445_road_(Ireland))___ ___E:regional road U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_road_(Ireland))___ and close to the ___E:M7 motorway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M7_motorway_(Ireland))___ , where Junction 23 provides access to the village.
___E:Bus Éireann U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_%C3%89ireann)___ no longer provides a service to Moneygall.

As of 2019, bus service 854, operated by ___E:Local Link U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TFI_Local_Link)___ Tipperary between ___E:Roscrea railway station U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscrea_railway_station)___ and Nenagh, called at Main Street and ___E:Obama Plaza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Plaza)___ .
The service operates seven days a week.

There is no train station in the village but the nearest stations are in ___E:Nenagh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nenagh)___ , ___E:Cloughjordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloughjordan)___ and ___E:Roscrea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscrea)___ , all on the ___E:Limerick-Ballybrophy railway line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limerick-Ballybrophy_railway_line)___ , a feeder service to the main ___E:Cork U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_(city))___ to ___E:Dublin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin)___ line, operated by ___E:Iarnród Éireann U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iarnr%C3%B3d_%C3%89ireann)___ .

The closest ___E:airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airport)___ with scheduled passenger services is ___E:Shannon Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Airport)___ in ___E:County Clare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Clare)___ .
There is one ___E:Catholic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic)___ ___E:national school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_school_(Ireland))___ in the village.

The former ___E:Church of Ireland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Ireland)___ school (now used as a parish hall) was built in 1888 beside the ___E:R490 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R490_road_(Ireland))___ ___E:Borrisokane U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borrisokane)___ turn-off, and closed in 1976, when its pupils were transferred to the neighbouring village of ___E:Cloughjordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloughjordan)___ .
An earlier building,  constructed around 1800, was previously used as a school.
It was then used by the local Church of Ireland community as a chapel of ease until the late 1970s.
It has now been converted to a private residence.
Children travel mainly to either ___E:Roscrea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscrea)___ or ___E:Nenagh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nenagh)___ for secondary schooling.

The nearest ___E:third-level institutions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education)___ are ___E:Tipperary Institute U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tipperary_Institute)___ in ___E:Thurles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thurles)___ or the ___E:University of Limerick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Limerick)___ , ___E:Limerick Institute of Technology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limerick_Institute_of_Technology)___ and ___E:Mary Immaculate College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Immaculate_College)___ , all of which are in ___E:Limerick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limerick)___ .

While all of the village is located in County Offaly, the ___E:Gaelic Athletic Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaelic_Athletic_Association)___ playing field is located in County Tipperary, and ___E:Moneygall GAA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moneygall_GAA)___ play in the Tipperary GAA Championships.
Moneygall FC opened its new grounds in 2017 in the centre of the village.
The club, while based in County Offaly, compete in North Tipperary. [citation needed]
As of the ___E:2016 census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_census_of_Ireland)___ , there were 313 people living in Moneygall.
The previous ___E:2011 census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census_of_Ireland_2011)___ counted 310 people in the village (153 males and 157 females).
This, in turn, was an increase of 12 people (4%) since the census of 2006.

Falmouth Kearney, a maternal great-great-great-grandfather of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , 44th ___E:President of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ , emigrated from Moneygall to ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ at the age of 19 in 1850 and eventually resettled in ___E:Tipton County, Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tipton_County,_Indiana)___ .
Kearney's father, Joseph, had been the village shoemaker.
The Kearney family emigrated to ___E:Ross County, Ohio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_County,_Ohio)___ , in the first half of the 19th century.

Falmouth Kearney's youngest daughter, Mary Ann, moved from Indiana to ___E:Kansas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas)___ after her father's death in 1878. Mary Ann Kearney was the paternal grandmother of ___E:Stanley Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Armour_Dunham)___ , President Obama's maternal grandfather.
On 23 May 2011, Obama and First Lady ___E:Michelle Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ , visited Moneygall as part of a visit to Ireland.
They were welcomed by 5,000 people and greeted upon arrival by the President's eighth cousin, Henry Healy.
Following a walkabout on the main street, where they shook hands with many local residents, the Obamas entered a house that had been built on the site where Falmouth Kearney had lived.
Afterwards, they visited Ollie Hayes's ___E:pub U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_pub)___ to meet more of the President's distant relatives and to study the birth records of his ancestors.

President and Mrs. Obama drank Irish ___E:stout U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stout)___ to the traditional toast, sláinte (meaning "good health"), and Mrs. Obama went behind the bar to learn how to pull a pint.

The Barack Obama Plaza service area was opened at Junction 23 of the ___E:M7 motorway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M7_motorway_(Ireland))___ on the outskirts of Moneygall in June 2014.  Life-sized bronze sculptures of Barack and Michelle Obama were added outside the Plaza in August 2018.
